govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAHughesHoward:
Playboy magazine, carrying a Chicago Sun-Times Service report, printed a remarkable claim: the CIA had considered using Howard Hughes's organization as a front to funnel money into American politics. The named targets were the 1968 campaigns of Gerald Ford and thirty other legislators.

The scheme, as reported, would have hidden the agency's hand behind the billionaire's empire, which already did business with the CIA. Nothing in the article says the plan was carried out; its news is that it was considered at all. The piece survives as an artifact of the seventies, when such plots were printable because some had proved true.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIWeisbergHaro: Harold Weisberg swore an affidavit in his Freedom of Information Act case against the General Services Administration, styled Weisberg v. General Services Administration. Weisberg spent years suing agencies for assassination records, and an affidavit put his account under oath. The surviving record identifies the document and the case but gives no date or contents, so it stands as a sworn filing from that records suit.
